admission-controller.md.title: Admission Controller: Kubernetes API Request Interception
admission-controller.md.summary: Explains Kubernetes admission controllers—configurable filters for API requests (validating/mutating) that can reject or modify objects before persistence. Covers their roles in security and policy enforcement.

admission-policies.md.title: Declarative Admission Policies in Kubernetes: Validating & Mutating
admission-policies.md.summary: Explains declarative admission policies in Kubernetes using CEL (Common Expression Language) for validation and mutation. Covers setup, policy types (Validating/Mutating), elements (policy/binding), and practical usage with examples like replica limits and label enforcement.

admission-webhooks-good-practices.md.title: Admission Webhook Best Practices for Kubernetes
admission-webhooks-good-practices.md.summary: This document outlines best practices for designing admission webhooks in Kubernetes, covering validation, mutation, performance, and failure prevention. It emphasizes careful design to avoid disruptions and compatibility issues with Kubernetes API changes.

affinity.md.title: Kubernetes Affinity Scheduling Rules
affinity.md.summary: Explains Kubernetes affinity rules for pod scheduling, covering node affinity and pod-to-pod affinity. Describes how labels and selectors influence placement with required/preferred enforcement.

aggregation-layer.md.title: Configuring Kubernetes Aggregation Layer for Custom APIs
aggregation-layer.md.summary: Explains how to install and configure the Kubernetes aggregation layer to add custom APIs by enabling `APIService` objects in the Kubernetes API Server.

annotation.md.title: What is an Annotation (Key-Value Metadata)
annotation.md.summary: Explains annotations as key-value metadata for attaching arbitrary non-identifying metadata to objects. Describes flexibility in structure and content for clients to retrieve metadata.

api-group.md.title: Understanding Kubernetes API Groups
api-group.md.summary: Explains Kubernetes API groups—sets of related paths in the Kubernetes API. Describes enabling/disabling groups via API server config and their role in API versioning and extension.

api-resource.md.title: Kubernetes API Resource: Endpoint and Schema Definition
api-resource.md.summary: Explains Kubernetes API resources as HTTP endpoints defining schemas for objects/operations. Covers their role in the Kubernetes type system and examples like permissions or object representations.

api-server-bypass-risks.md.title: Kubernetes API Server Bypass Risks: Static Pods, kubelet API, etcd API, and Runtime Socket Exploits
api-server-bypass-risks.md.summary: Explains risks of bypassing Kubernetes API server controls via static Pods, kubelet API, etcd API, and container runtime socket manipulation. Details attack vectors, restrictions, and mitigation strategies for cluster operators and security architects.

app-container.md.title: App Container in Kubernetes Pods
app-container.md.summary: Explains the role of app containers within Kubernetes pods, distinguishing them from init containers and detailing their lifecycle after initialization tasks complete.

application-architect.md.title: Role of the Application Architect
application-architect.md.summary: Explains the role of an Application Architect in designing scalable, maintainable app implementations. Covers interactions with databases, microservices, and infrastructure components.

application-security-checklist.md.title: Kubernetes Application Security Checklist for Developers
application-security-checklist.md.summary: A developer-focused checklist for securing Kubernetes applications, covering base hardening, security contexts, RBAC, image security, and network policies. Focuses on best practices for pod/container-level security and application design.
topics: Service accounts (avoiding default, automount token control)

approver.md.title: Role of Approvers in Kubernetes Code Contributions
approver.md.summary: Explains the distinction between code review and approval in Kubernetes contributions. Approvers validate holistic acceptance (compatibility, conventions, performance, system interactions) for scoped codebases, replacing the term 'maintainers'.

architecture.md.title: Kubernetes Cluster Architecture Overview
architecture.md.summary: Describes the core components of a Kubernetes cluster, including control plane (kube-apiserver, etcd, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, cloud-controller-manager) and node components (kubelet, kube-proxy, container runtime). Explains fault tolerance, high availability, and deployment variations.

authentication-mechanisms.md.title: Authentication Mechanisms Hardening Guide
authentication-mechanisms.md.summary: Guide on hardening authentication mechanisms in Kubernetes, detailing security considerations for X.509 client certificates, static token files, and other methods. Focuses on minimizing authentication sources and auditing credential sources for production clusters.

authorization.md.title: Kubernetes Authorization: Request Verification and Policy Enforcement
authorization.md.summary: Explains Kubernetes authorization mechanics, including how request verdicts (allow/deny) are determined, request attributes used, and authorization modes. Covers configuration via config files or CLI flags, and details about privilege escalation via workload operations.

autoscaling.md.title: Kubernetes Autoscaling Strategies
autoscaling.md.summary: Explains manual and automatic scaling techniques in Kubernetes, covering horizontal and vertical scaling methods, including HPA, VPA, and their configurations. Highlights limitations like in-place pod resizing for VPA.
topics: Manual scaling via `kubectl` and resource patching

cadvisor.md.title: cAdvisor: Container Resource Monitoring and Metrics Collection
cadvisor.md.summary: Explains cAdvisor's role in monitoring container resource usage, collecting metrics like CPU, memory, and network stats, and exporting aggregated data for container and machine-wide analysis.

cdi.md.title: Container Device Interface (CDI) Specification
cdi.md.summary: Explains the Container Device Interface (CDI) specification for configuring devices inside Kubernetes containers, detailing its integration with device plugins and dynamic resource allocation for workload setup (e.g., bind mounts, environment variables).

cel.md.title: Common Expression Language (CEL) – Kubernetes
cel.md.summary: Explains CEL, a fast, portable, and safe expression language for Kubernetes. Details its use in dynamic admission control and dynamic resource allocation.

certificate.md.title: Kubernetes Cluster Certificate Authentication
certificate.md.summary: Explains the role of cryptographic certificates in securing Kubernetes API access. Describes how certificates validate client authentication within the cluster.

cgroup.md.title: Linux cgroup: Resource Management for Process Groups
cgroup.md.summary: Explains Linux cgroup, a kernel feature for isolating and limiting CPU, memory, I/O, and network usage of process groups. Details resource accounting and management techniques.

cidr.md.title: CIDR in Kubernetes Networking
cidr.md.summary: Explains CIDR (Classless Inter-Domain Routing) for IP address allocation in Kubernetes, detailing its use in assigning Node and Pod IPs via subnet masks (IPv4/IPv6).

cla.md.title: Contributor License Agreement (CLA) - Legal Terms for Open Source Contributions
cla.md.summary: Describes the legal framework for contributors granting open-source project licenses to their code/IP. Ensures IP rights and dispute resolution for contributions.

cloud-controller-manager.md.title: Cloud Controller Manager: Kubernetes Cloud-Specific Control Plane Component
cloud-controller-manager.md.summary: Explains the Cloud Controller Manager (CCM) as a Kubernetes control plane component embedding cloud-specific logic. It decouples cloud provider interactions from the cluster, enabling independent feature evolution between Kubernetes and cloud providers.

cloud-native-security.md.title: Kubernetes Cloud Native Security Lifecycle Guide
cloud-native-security.md.summary: Explains cloud native security practices across Kubernetes lifecycle phases (Develop, Distribute, Deploy, Runtime). Covers security controls, threat modeling, supply chain security, and runtime protection strategies.

cloud-provider.md.title: Understanding Cloud Providers and Cloud Services
cloud-provider.md.summary: Explains what cloud providers (CSPs) are, their roles in cloud computing, and the different service models (IaaS, PaaS). Highlights managed infrastructure and Kubernetes services, including responsibilities of cloud providers vs. users.

cluster-administration.md.title: Cluster Administration: Kubernetes Setup and Management Guide
cluster-administration.md.summary: This document provides an overview of Kubernetes cluster administration, covering planning, setup, and management. It includes considerations for choosing distros, managing nodes, securing clusters, and optional services like networking and authentication.

cluster-operations.md.title: Cluster Operations: Kubernetes Cluster Management Guide
cluster-operations.md.summary: This document outlines day-to-day Kubernetes cluster management tasks, including scaling, upgrades, security, networking, and observability. It covers operational workflows for coordinating cluster operations efficiently.

cluster-operator.md.title: Role of Cluster Operator
cluster-operator.md.summary: Describes the responsibilities of a **Cluster Operator**, focusing on cluster management, maintenance, and monitoring. Distinguishes them from the Kubernetes Operator pattern.

cluster.md.title: Understanding Kubernetes Cluster Architecture
cluster.md.summary: Explains Kubernetes cluster basics: nodes, Pods, control plane, and fault-tolerance. Describes worker nodes, Pod management, and production-grade scaling for HA.

cncf.md.title: Overview of the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF)
cncf.md.summary: Explains CNCF’s role in promoting cloud-native computing ecosystems, particularly around containers and microservices. Highlights Kubernetes as a key CNCF project under the Linux Foundation’s umbrella.

cni.md.title: Container Network Interface (CNI) Plugin Specification
cni.md.summary: Explains CNI plugins as CNI-compliant network interfaces for containers, detailing their role in Kubernetes networking and adherence to the appc/CNI specification.

components.md.title: Kubernetes Cluster Architecture Overview
components.md.summary: Explains Kubernetes core components (control plane, nodes) and add-ons (DNS, monitoring, logging). Highlights flexibility in deployment for varying environments.

condition.md.title: Kubernetes Resource Conditions: Standardized Status Reporting
condition.md.summary: Explains Kubernetes conditions—fields in resource statuses—that describe resource states (e.g., Pod readiness). Covers `type`, `status` (True/False/Unknown), `reason`, and `message` fields for standardized communication between components.

configuration.md.title: Kubernetes Configuration Methods: APIs, ConfigMaps, Secrets, and Helper Containers
configuration.md.summary: Explains Kubernetes configuration approaches, including APIs (ConfigMaps/Secrets), sidecar/init containers, and filesystem/env variables. Focuses on separating config from code for reusability and security in cloud-native environments.

container-env-variables.md.title: Container Environment Variables: Use Cases and Best Practices
container-env-variables.md.summary: Explains how to configure and use environment variables in containers, covering their purpose (e.g., app settings, cluster metadata) and best practices for deployment and management.

container-runtime.md.title: Container Runtime: Kubernetes CRI Overview
container-runtime.md.summary: Explains Kubernetes' Container Runtime Interface (CRI) and supported runtimes like containerd and crio. Details how Kubernetes manages container lifecycle via CRI implementations.

container.md.title: What is a Container? – Containerization Basics
container.md.summary: Explains containers as lightweight, portable executable images bundling software and dependencies. Details how containers decouple apps from infrastructure for easier deployment and scaling across environments.

containerd.md.title: containerd: Container Runtime Documentation
containerd.md.summary: Explains containerd’s architecture, core features (image management, container execution, networking), and its role as a lightweight, portable container runtime for Linux/Windows. Focuses on technical design and operational aspects.
